Yes. AMD’s FY22 quick ratio was approximately 1.49, calculated as cash and equivalents plus short-term investments plus accounts receivable divided by current liabilities, indicating a reasonably healthy liquidity profile because quick assets exceeded current liabilities.

As of FY22, AMD’s major products and services included x86 microprocessors/accelerated processing units for servers, desktops and notebooks; graphics processing units; chipsets; semi-custom system-on-chip products for game consoles; adaptive SoCs/FPGAs and other embedded processors; and related development services.

AMD’s FY22 revenue increase was driven primarily by much higher Embedded revenue from the Xilinx acquisition and strong Data Center growth from EPYC server processor sales; Gaming also rose modestly, while Client revenue declined due to weaker PC demand.

AMD’s FY22 GAAP operating margin fell to about 5% from about 22% in FY21, driven primarily by amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the Xilinx acquisition and higher R&D and SG&A expenses, partly offset by higher gross profit from revenue growth. Operating margin remains useful, but FY22 GAAP comparability is affected by acquisition-related amortization and integration-related costs.
